fields.hypothesis: A post-deposition aging heat treatment to refine the Mo-induced σ-phase dispersion will enhance mechanical strength, room‐temperature creep resistance, and corrosion resistance.
fields.material_initial_state: DED-fabricated CrCoNiFeMo high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase (FCC + σ) microstructure as produced by powder blending with 5–10% Mo addition.
fields.intervention: Apply a two-step heat treatment: first a solution treatment to homogenize the alloy followed by a short-duration aging (e.g., at ~700 °C for 1 hour) to precipitate a fine, uniformly distributed Mo-rich σ phase.
fields.conditions: Heat treatment carried out in an inert atmosphere; aging parameters tuned to avoid over-coarsening, under conditions similar to precipitation hardening treatments (e.g., analogous to A286 treatment regimes) while ensuring the alloy remains in the desired dual-phase balance at room temperature.
fields.structural_mediator: Uniform, nanometer-to-micrometer scale Mo-rich σ phase precipitates dispersed along grain boundaries and within grains.
fields.mechanism: The fine σ-phase precipitates increase grain boundary pinning and dislocation obstruction, thereby raising yield and ultimate tensile strengths while simultaneously impeding dislocation motion responsible for room-temperature creep. Additionally, the refined microstructure reduces the number of active corrosion sites, enhancing passivation in corrosive environments such as 3.5 wt% NaCl.
fields.predicted_outcome: Compared to the as-deposited alloy, an increase in yield strength (potentially in the range of an additional 10–20% improvement over the untreated state), reduced room-temperature creep under service loads, and lower corrosion current density (Icorr) in electrochemical tests.
fields.baseline: As-deposited DED HEA with already improved properties from Mo alloying but without any post-processing heat treatment.
fields.boundary: Excessive aging time or temperature may coarsen the σ phase too much, leading to embrittlement and degraded ductility. The intervention is optimized only within a narrow aging parameter window.
fields.uncertainty: The optimal aging parameters (time and temperature) for achieving the finest σ-phase dispersion while maintaining ductility under operational conditions remain to be precisely determined.

Perform standardized tensile tests, room-temperature creep tests under constant load, and potentiodynamic polarization tests in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
measurements: Yield and ultimate tensile strength
Creep strain over time under a fixed load
Corrosion potential (Ecorr) and corrosion current density (Icorr)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated specimens do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in strength (>=10% increase), lower creep strain rate, and improved corrosion metrics (higher Ecorr and lower Icorr) compared to the untreated baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.

pool.what_is_new: Introduces laser shock peening—a surface treatment not explored in the paper—as a single, post-fabrication mechanical intervention to further enhance durability, creep resistance, and corrosion performance of HEA fasteners.

fields.hypothesis: Application of laser shock peening (LSP) to the surface of the DED-fabricated Mo-containing HEA will improve its mechanical durability, room‐temperature creep resistance, and corrosion resistance.
fields.material_initial_state: DED-manufactured high-entropy alloy fasteners containing Mo with a dual-phase FCC + σ microstructure, which may display surface tensile residual stresses and microstructural irregularities from the additive process.
fields.intervention: Perform laser shock peening on the as-fabricated components using optimized laser parameters to impart deep compressive residual stresses and slightly refine the surface grain structure without altering the bulk phase composition.
fields.conditions: LSP performed at ambient temperature with controlled laser energy and coverage to avoid surface over-peening; the process is applied uniformly on fastener surfaces in air or controlled atmosphere.
fields.structural_mediator: A near-surface microstructure characterized by increased compressive residual stresses and a refined grain size, potentially with reduced surface defects.
fields.mechanism: The compressive residual stresses induced by LSP inhibit crack initiation and retard dislocation motion, thereby reducing room-temperature creep and fatigue. Moreover, the refined surface microstructure reduces the number and size of corrosion initiation sites, leading to enhanced corrosion resistance. Collectively, these factors improve the mechanical durability of fasteners under cyclic and static loads.
fields.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated specimens, LSP-treated fasteners should exhibit higher fatigue strength, a measurable reduction in creep strain under constant load, and improved corrosion behavior (elevated Ecorr and reduced Icorr) in salt-spray or electrochemical tests.
fields.baseline: As-deposited DED HEA fasteners with Mo addition, possessing the inherent dual-phase structure but without any post-fabrication surface stress modification.
fields.boundary: If laser parameters are not optimized, over-peening may lead to excessive surface roughness or micro-cracking, which would negate the benefits; the effects are primarily near the surface (depth limited).
fields.uncertainty: The magnitude of improvement in room-temperature creep behavior and corrosion resistance specific to this HEA, as well as the depth of beneficial compressive stress, may vary with LSP process parameters.

Characterize surface residual stresses (using X-ray diffraction), perform microstructural analysis (via EBSD or SEM), and conduct fatigue, creep (under constant load at room temperature), and corrosion testing (potentiodynamic polarization in NaCl solution).
measurements: Compressive residual stress magnitude and depth profile
Surface grain size and defect density
Fatigue life and creep strain measurements
Ecorr and Icorr from corrosion tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no statistically significant improvements in compressive residual stress, fatigue/creep resistance, or corrosion resistance are observed in the LSP-treated samples compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.

pool.builds_on: The paper’s discussion of grain size effects, including the inverse Hall–Petch phenomenon observed for excessively fine grains, underlines the importance of microstructural control. This hypothesis uses that insight to propose a gradient grain structure that capitalizes on both fine and coarse grain benefits.
pool.what_is_new: Distinct from the paper’s parameter studies, this proposal employs a single, integrated thermo-mechanical processing intervention to intentionally create a bimodal microstructure that could balance and optimize mechanical durability, creep resistance, and corrosion performance in aerospace fasteners.

fields.hypothesis: A controlled thermo-mechanical processing route designed to produce a bimodal (gradient) grain size distribution in the HEA will enhance mechanical durability, improve room-temperature creep resistance, and boost corrosion resistance in aerospace fasteners.
fields.material_initial_state: As-cast Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18 HEA with a homogeneous grain structure.

top3.label: C1
top3.builds_on: the established concept in superalloy literature that trace additions of reactive elements (e.g., Y) segregate to grain boundaries to improve interfacial cohesion and oxidation resistance.
top3.what_is_new: This approach proposes a minor compositional modification as a single intervention to achieve simultaneous improvements in room-temperature mechanical properties, creep resistance, and corrosion behavior in HEAs used for aerospace fasteners—a route not explored in the original paper.

fields.hypothesis: Slightly modify the alloy composition by adding a controlled trace amount of a grain boundary segregant (e.g., yttrium) to enhance grain boundary cohesion and promote the formation of protective oxides, thus improving mechanical durability, room-temperature creep resistance, and corrosion resistance.
fields.material_initial_state: SLM‐fabricated HEA with a baseline composition currently containing minor elements including B (0.01 wt.%) but without intentional additions of reactive rare-earth elements.
fields.intervention: Introduce an additional trace element, such as 0.05 wt.% yttrium, into the prealloyed powder prior to gas atomization or by surface coating and subsequent diffusion treatment. This addition is designed to segregate to the grain boundaries during subsequent processing and heat treatment.
fields.conditions: The modified alloy processing follows the same solution treatment (≥1120°C) and heat treatment schedule as the baseline HEA, ensuring that during cooling and aging, Y atoms preferentially segregate to the grain boundaries. The addition is low enough not to disturb the overall phase equilibria yet sufficient to influence interfacial chemistry. This intervention is intended for HEAs used in aerospace fasteners operating at room temperature.
fields.structural_mediator: Enhanced grain boundary cohesion and stability due to yttrium segregation at the boundaries, plus the promotion of a more adherent and protective oxide layer at the boundaries.
fields.mechanism: Yttrium is known in superalloys to segregate to grain boundaries where it improves cohesion and retards the initiation and propagation of intergranular cracks. It can also lead to the formation of a finely adherent Y-rich oxide during exposure to oxidizing environments, which stabilizes the passive film. Together, these effects can reduce creep deformation at room temperature by limiting dislocation motion along weak interfaces and improve corrosion resistance by minimizing localized corrosion attack at the grain boundaries.
fields.predicted_outcome: Compared with the baseline HEA, the yttrium-doped alloy is expected to exhibit enhanced mechanical durability (e.g., a measurable reduction in propagation of intergranular cracks under cyclic loading), lower room-temperature creep strain under sustained load (improved by a quantifiable margin, tentatively on the order of 20%), and improved corrosion metrics (such as lower corrosion current densities from electrochemical tests).
fields.baseline: HEA processed with the original composition and standard heat treatment without any intentional grain boundary segregant addition.
fields.boundary: The improvement is sensitive to the precise Y content; too little may have no effect, whereas too much might lead to the formation of unwanted Y-rich phases that could embrittle the alloy. Control over Y distribution is critical.
fields.uncertainty: While grain boundary segregation of reactive elements like Y is well-established in nickel-based superalloys, direct quantitative correlation in HEAs at room temperature is less documented, so the exact magnitude of the improvements remains to be determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of HEA specimens: one with the standard composition and one with an additional 0.05 wt.% Y. Ensure identical SLM fabrication and heat treatments. Use atom probe tomography or TEM-EDS to verify Y segregation at grain boundaries. Then, perform room-temperature creep tests, fatigue/durability assessments, and corrosion tests (e.g., potentiodynamic polarization) to compare the performance.
measurements: Quantification of Y segregation at grain boundaries via microanalysis
Room-temperature creep strain and fatigue life measurements
Corrosion parameters such as corrosion current density and passivation behavior
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yttrium-enhanced specimens do not show a statistically significant improvement (for example, >20% gain in durability or creep resistance and improved corrosion metrics) relative to the baseline, or if deleterious secondary phases form, the hypothesis is falsified.

top3.label: C10
top3.builds_on: the established high corrosion resistance of electrospark deposited HfNbTaTiZr HEA coatings (PMC8348113) and leverages known alumina-passivation benefits from studies on nickel aluminide and superalloys.
top3.what_is_new: This hypothesis introduces a compositional adjustment (Al addition) with explicit prior thermodynamic calibration to ensure phase stability, targeting a simultaneous enhancement in corrosion protection, mechanical durability, and creep resistance in an aerospace fastener application.

fields.hypothesis: Introducing a minor 3–5 at.% Al addition into the HfNbTaTiZr HEA, with prior thermodynamic calibration to ensure BCC phase stability, to promote the in situ formation of a thin, adherent alumina (Al2O3) passivation layer without destabilizing the structure.
fields.material_initial_state: The base material is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr HEA processed via mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and electrospark deposition, exhibiting a predominantly BCC structure with high corrosion resistance and good mechanical properties.
fields.intervention: Modify the alloy composition to include 3–5 at.% Al by pre-mixing the appropriate elemental powders followed by the same processing route (mechanical alloying, SPS consolidation, and electrospark deposition). Prior to full-scale processing, use thermodynamic modeling and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to confirm that the added Al will not destabilize the BCC phase.
fields.conditions: Maintain the conventional processing parameters in an inert (argon) atmosphere throughout alloying and coating deposition. Verify the composition and phase stability at ambient temperature as found in aerospace fastener operational environments (room temperature with aggressive corrosive agents).
fields.structural_mediator: The controlled Al addition is anticipated to segregate subtly to the surface during electrospark deposition and service, forming a continuous, nanometric Al2O3 layer while remaining in solid solution in the interior to yield solid-solution strengthening.
fields.mechanism: Owing to its high oxygen affinity, Al will react with trace oxygen during service or minor post-deposition oxidation to form a stable alumina film that acts as a barrier against corrosion. Simultaneously, the dissolved Al atoms provide solid-solution strengthening, thereby reducing dislocation mobility that contributes to room-temperature creep. Thermodynamic validations ensure that the desired BCC structure is preserved without forming brittle intermetallics.
fields.predicted_outcome: Relative to the untreated HEA, the Al-modified HEA should display lower corrosion current density (icorr) due to an effective passivation layer, improved surface hardness, and a modest reduction in creep strain rate. The expected improvements are moderate but statistically significant, pending quantitative experimental validation.
fields.baseline: Untreated HfNbTaTiZr HEA produced via the described processing route, as characterized in PMC8348113.
fields.boundary: The beneficial effects depend on maintaining a low Al content; exceeding ~5 at.% could induce unwanted phase transformations or embrittlement. The preliminary thermodynamic analysis and DSC tests are essential to determine the safe compositional window.
fields.uncertainty: Uncertainty remains regarding the precise segregation behavior of Al during rapid cooling and whether the alumina layer will form uniformly without compromising the overall BCC stability. Quantitative improvement magnitudes require experimental confirmation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sample sets: one using standard HfNbTaTiZr and one with an added 3–5 at.% Al. Validate phase stability via XRD and DSC. Process both via identical mechanical alloying, SPS, and electrospark deposition. Subject them to standardized corrosion tests in 3.5% NaCl solution and room-temperature creep tests under fixed load.
measurements: XRD and DSC for phase confirmation
Electrochemical measurements (Ecorr, icorr) via Tafel analysis
Microhardness and creep strain measurements under controlled load
SEM/EDS to verify the formation and continuity of the alumina layer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-modified HEA does not exhibit statistically significant improvements in corrosion resistance (lower icorr), enhanced hardness, or reduced room-temperature creep relative to the baseline—or if microstructural characterization reveals destabilization of the BCC phase—the hypothesis is falsified.

top3.label: C13
top3.builds_on: the observed benefits of nanoscale carbide dispersion and twin-induced plasticity in the dual-phase HEA from PMC5227964, extending the strategy by introducing a heat-treatment step to further refine and stabilize the nano-constituent framework.
top3.what_is_new: It proposes a novel post–cold-rolling low-temperature short-time annealing treatment to optimize the dispersion of strengthening nano-carbides, specifically targeting improvements in room-temperature creep and corrosion resistance, an intervention not discussed in the original study.

fields.hypothesis: Tailored Low-Temperature Short-Time Annealing to Stabilize Nano-Precipitate Dispersion and Enhance Creep and Corrosion Performance
fields.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy processed as in PMC5227964 with dual-phase microstructure comprising an f.c.c. matrix, interstitial carbon, and nano-carbide precipitates formed during standard thermomechanical processing.
fields.intervention: Introduce an additional heat treatment step consisting of a very short (e.g., 1–3 minutes) annealing at a lower temperature (around 700°C) immediately after cold rolling, followed by rapid quenching.
fields.conditions: The alloy is produced by the same melting and thermomechanical route as in PMC5227964, but after cold rolling the specimen is annealed at 700°C for a precisely controlled short time in an inert atmosphere (e.g., argon) to prevent oxidation, then water-quenched.
fields.structural_mediator: This annealing is designed to further refine and homogenize the distribution of nano-carbides (M23C6) without promoting their coarsening, thereby maintaining a high density of obstacles (particles) within the f.c.c. matrix.
fields.mechanism: At lower annealing temperatures and short times, diffusion of substitutional and interstitial atoms is limited, preventing significant growth of precipitates while relieving residual stresses and promoting a uniform dispersion of nano-carbides. The fine carbide dispersion enhances dislocation pinning (through an Orowan mechanism) and retards grain boundary sliding, thus improving room-temperature creep resistance. In addition, a uniform and refined microstructure can lead to a more homogeneous passive surface film that is less prone to localized corrosion attack.
fields.predicted_outcome: Modest improvements (expected in the range of 10–20%) in yield and tensile strengths and a noticeable decrease in room-temperature creep strain under constant load, along with enhanced corrosion resistance (evidenced by a reduced corrosion current density) relative to the baseline processing route.
fields.baseline: The standard interstitial TWIP-TRIP‑HEA processed as described in PMC5227964 without the additional low-temperature annealing step.
fields.boundary: Too low a temperature or an excessively short annealing time may not sufficiently homogenize the nano-carbide dispersion, while too high a temperature or longer times could lead to carbide coarsening and loss of strengthening benefits. Thus, precise control is essential.
fields.uncertainty: The optimal annealing parameters (temperature and time) need to be determined; the quantitative improvements may vary with slight deviations in the processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of HEA specimens: one using the standard processing route (as in PMC5227964) and one with the additional low-temperature, short-time annealing. Characterize the nano-precipitate size and distribution (using TEM or APT) and perform room-temperature tensile and creep tests along with corrosion tests (potentiodynamic polarization).
measurements: Grain and precipitate size distributions
Tensile properties including yield and ultimate strength
Creep strain under a fixed constant load over time
Corrosion current density and potential
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified heat-treated samples fail to show significant improvements in nano-precipitate uniformity, mechanical durability, creep resistance, and corrosion behavior compared to the standard samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
